transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah. I guess the main reason I came in is because at work I keep getting up when I’m not supposed to. Like, I’m a production worker, so I’m supposed to stay at my station, and I know that, but I’ll just suddenly leave it or pop up during meetings like I need to move right then. It’s not like I plan it out or think, “I’m going to walk away now.” It’s more like my body goes before my brain catches up.

My supervisor has been on me about it because it’s starting to be a safety issue. Like, I’ll take off from where I’m supposed to be before I even really think through whether it’s okay, and then afterward I’m like, “Why did I just do that?” It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not trying to cause problems or ignore rules, but I keep doing it, and now it’s gotten bad enough that they’re saying it can’t keep happening.
Right before you get up or move, do you notice any physical sensation—like tension, restlessness, or an uncomfortable feeling in your legs or body—that gets better once you move?

Yeah, I do. It’s like this pressure building up in my body, if that makes sense. Like if I’m standing still by the machine and I’m supposed to just stay there and keep doing the same thing, after a little bit I start feeling like I’m almost crawling inside my own skin. Not pain exactly, but like my body is saying, “Move, move, move,” and it gets louder the longer I try to ignore it.

Same thing if I’m sitting through training or a meeting. I’ll try to sit normal and listen, but then I start shifting around, stretching my legs, moving my hands, whatever, and it still feels like I need to get up right then. And when I finally do move—like pace for a second or stretch or go do something—it does feel better, at least for a little while. It’s just really hard to make myself stay still when that feeling starts.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started, any antipsychotic medications, anti-nausea drugs, or other new prescriptions?

Um… I don’t think so. I’m not on anything like that, at least not that I know of. Nobody’s put me on some new prescription recently or anything for nausea or, like, those kinds of meds you mentioned.

I mean, I’m not always great with the names of medications, honestly, so if you mean something specific I might need you to say the brand name or what it’s usually for. But I haven’t started anything new lately that I can think of.
Is this restless, need-to-move feeling mainly in your legs and worse in the evening or at night, or does it happen throughout your whole body at any time of day?

It’s not really just my legs, no. I mean, my legs are part of it, because I’ll stretch them or bounce them or feel like I need to walk, but it feels more like my whole body gets wound up.

Like if I’m standing by the machine and I’m supposed to stay in one spot, it’s this pressure that builds up in me, like I have to move right then. Or if I’m sitting through training, I’ll start shifting around and then it turns into needing to pace or stretch or go do something. It’s not only at night or anything like that. It can happen during the day at work, during meetings, training—kind of whenever I’m expected to stay still.
Has this need to move and feeling restless been something you've dealt with since you were a kid, or is this more of a new thing that's started recently?

No, it’s definitely not new. I mean, it feels like it’s been me my whole life, honestly. Even in elementary school I was that kid who could not stay in my seat. Like I’d be up wandering around the room when we were supposed to be doing work, or I’d be turning around talking, or just blurting stuff out before the teacher was done talking.

I remember getting notes sent home a lot for that kind of thing—talking over the teacher, interrupting, not staying where I was supposed to stay. It wasn’t like I was trying to be bad every time, I just… I don’t know, I felt like I had to move or say the thing right then. So yeah, this has been around since I was little, not something that just started recently.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong (since elementary school) pattern of motor restlessness, inability to remain seated, impulsive movement, blurting out, and interrupting others, consistent with childhood-onset hyperactive-impulsive symptoms. Current presentation shows persistence into adulthood with functional impairment (workplace safety issue, supervisor complaints) across multiple settings (work station, meetings, training). Restless leg syndrome and akathisia were considered given the described urge-to-move sensation relieved by movement, but these were ruled out: symptoms are not confined to the legs, not worse specifically at night, and there is no history of new antipsychotic, antiemetic, or other akathisia-inducing medication exposure. The chronic developmental trajectory (present since early childhood, cross-situational, associated with classic ADHD hyperactive/impulsive behaviors) best fits ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation, unspecified type.
